title: Founded Bridgewater Associates from a two-bedroom Manhattan apartment
statement: Founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975 out of his two-bedroom New York City apartment, advising corporate clients carried over from his Shearson Hayden Stone commodities career and publishing the Daily Observations research letter.
outcome: Bridgewater grew into the world's largest hedge fund, managing about $150 billion at its 2016 peak and pioneering risk parity, alpha-beta separation, and currency overlay.

title: Bet on a downturn after the Mexican debt default and lost his clients' money
statement: Concluded from the Latin American debt crisis that the U.S. economy and stock market would fall sharply, and positioned himself and his clients for the collapse.
outcome: The economy and market rose sharply instead; Dalio lost his own and his clients' money and had to borrow $4,000 from his father, an experience he calls the best thing that ever happened to him and the origin of his error-friendly, humility-driven culture.

title: Launched All Weather and pioneered risk parity
statement: Launched the All Weather fund in 1996, beginning as his own family trust and pioneering the risk parity approach that balances risk across economic environments rather than allocating capital by asset class.
outcome: Risk parity was adopted across the investment industry; the All Weather fund held more than $46 billion by 2011, and the All Weather China fund launched in 2018 grew to $5.5 billion by January 2024.

title: Self-published Principles as a free download
statement: Self-published a 123-page volume of his investment and management principles in 2011 and distributed it free, after a 2005 internal handbook had codified the culture at Bridgewater.
outcome: The free document drew more than three million downloads and became the basis for Principles: Life & Work (2017), a New York Times number one bestseller that sold more than five million copies worldwide.

title: Stepped down as co-CEO in the management shakeup
statement: Announced in March 2017 that he would step down as Bridgewater's co-chief executive by April 15, as part of a company-wide management shakeup.
outcome: The co-CEO structure under Greg Jensen, Eileen Murray, and David McCormick took over; McCormick became sole CEO by 2020 and left in January 2022 to run for Senate, with Nir Bar Dea and Mark Bertolini named the next co-CEOs.

title: Gave away Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises
statement: Released A Template for Understanding Big Debt Crises as a free PDF in September 2018, ten years after the Lehman collapse, sharing the firm's internal template for how debt cycles work.
outcome: The template covered all 48 major debt crises of the previous 100 years and codified the framework behind Bridgewater's well-documented navigation of the 2008 crisis.

title: Launched Bridgewater's first onshore China fund
statement: After receiving Chinese regulatory approval in June 2018, launched Bridgewater All Weather China Private Fund Number 1 in October 2018, the firm's first domestic product for qualified Chinese investors.
outcome: The fund grew to $5.5 billion in assets by January 2024, extending the risk parity franchise into the Chinese institutional market.

title: Published Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order
statement: Published his study of the rise and decline of reserve-currency empires over 500 years, arguing that debt creation and money printing, internal conflict from record wealth gaps, and China's challenge to American power were converging.
outcome: The book extended into How Countries Go Broke (2025), a New York Times bestseller, and its framework was debated publicly alongside Henry Kissinger at a CSIS book event.

title: The 1982 'depression' call and public humiliation
statement: After Mexico's August 1982 default, Dalio publicly predicted a depression — the standard historical reading of a debt crisis — and staked client positions on it.
outcome: The Fed cut rates instead, the greatest bull market in bonds and equities in history began, and Dalio lost nearly everything including his staff. He calls it the best thing that happened to him: it taught him humility and led directly to the Bridgewater systemization of decision-making.

title: Systematizing Bridgewater around written principles
statement: Dalio codified the firm's decision rules as written 'Principles' — an idea-meritocracy with believability weighting, radical transparency and systematic disagreement — after realizing his own judgment could not scale without being made explicit.
outcome: The principles system ran the largest hedge fund in the world through decades of leadership transitions and was published as a book in 2017, becoming a business-management bestseller.

title: Institutionalizing Pure Alpha with separate client accounts
statement: Bridgewater rejected the pooled hedge-fund structure for separately managed institutional accounts, letting each client's risk preferences be expressed in their own mandate.
outcome: The structure helped Bridgewater become the first truly institutional hedge fund and ultimately the largest, managing roughly $150 billion at peak.

title: The 'depression gauge' that kept Bridgewater whole in 2008
statement: Bridgewater's systematic framework — built after the 1982 humiliation — flagged the 2008 arrangement as a classic deleveraging, and the Pure Alpha portfolios were positioned for it.
outcome: While the average hedge fund lost double digits, Bridgewater's flagship strategies returned roughly 9-14% in 2008, the defining proof of the systemization Dalio had built from his worst mistake.

title: Selling most of the family's gold — the contrarian exit
statement: After recommending gold for years as the ultimate deleveraging hedge, Dalio publicly noted in 2011-2012 that the precious-metal trade had become crowded and reduced exposure.
outcome: Gold entered a multi-year bear market from its 2011 peak near $1,900; the call illustrated his framework's application beyond debt — even correct theses become dangerous when consensus.

title: The Beijing advisory role and China immersion
statement: Dalio began advising Chinese institutions from the early 1990s and built Bridgewater's Beijing presence decades before other Western managers were allowed in.
outcome: Bridgewater became one of the first foreign managers to raise a onshore China fund in 2021; Dalio's China advocacy made him simultaneously a bridge figure and a political lightning rod in the US.
